author: Jurij
text:
Bodo, there is no right wrong. I understand your view. I saw the
opportunity for a setup by looking on what flag limits/FTRs are
important. For me your FTR3 is not important because it did not break
anything on the left (on that scale).

Price made a range (a box), meaning price flagged between two FTRs.

Once price broke out to the upside from that range it made an FTR, a decision that price was to cheap below.

Once this FTR breaks, the decision is made that price is no longer cheap
 and price is free to move to the other FTR which caused price to flag
previously in that range (previous decision point that price was too
cheap).

The PAZ between those 2 FTRs

This is how I draw the SPAZ

Does it help to understand better my view?

Personally for my own case, i
won't know if price will come back down to your Stacked demand PAZ
unless price was not able to engulf the supply but engulfed the FL2,
which did happened later.

Did i miss something important or my labels of DP were wrong?

The
 stacked demand zone was not involved to see the trade opportunity
because at that time the SPAZ wasn't there yet. Only the demand which is
 a reaction to your FTR3 made it a SPAZ. And there are no clues that
price will go to the other end of the SPAZ until price engulfs the
latest demand (tip of PAZ).

Yes engulf of your FL2 is also a good opportunity.

Hi bodo, FTR forms after a break not before, see this chart. Your FTR3 formed before the break of the flag limit (true supply).

Ah I think this confusion comes from decision points (DP) vs FTRs.
Decision points (DP) can be before a break, so you can say FTR3 is a
decision point to break the supply, but not an FTR.

Bodostock wrote: By the way, when you said " in its scale", you mean the H4 timeframe?

Yes, with scale I mean time frame but also in relation to important FTRs and swings.

On LTF there are other swings and FTRs but those don't matter in this
time frame in this context (scale) of those 2 FTRs that limit the flag
and created that range and PAZ.

Bodostock wrote: Anyway zooming
into the H1 timeframe, i now see that a paz zone was created after the
FL2 was created. This PAZ is between FL1 and FL2,

Yes very good, now we are on the same page. If FTR2 breaks price can move to FTR1 because that is the origin on this scale.

Bodostock wrote: And also now i
see your point why you said price did not manage to reach the other end
of the edge. Indeed it did not.
